hypothesis: Holding each native HIP-3 Swing direction and feature identity fixed while delaying entry to a next-bar confirmation or fast-EMA pullback, or limiting the state recipe to one entry per alignment episode, can improve after-cost development and validation economics without adding a market or side gate.
decision: Reject next-bar confirmation and fast-EMA pullback: confirmation worsened aggregate validation and the pullback eliminated nearly every trade. Keep v25 live timing unchanged. Retain only the SPCX alignment-episode onset arm as annotation-only because it removed four nominal and five stress development stop-out re-entries while leaving validation economics effectively unchanged. Do not add static side gates because SPCX, GOLD, and SNDK direction results rotated between development and validation. Require routed provider-episode and re-entry-ordinal evidence before considering a future flat-boundary onset profile. This revision cannot place, close, resize, route, gate, restart, or promote a strategy.
falsifier: Reject the onset candidate if routed wall-clock replay or forward annotation shows same-episode re-entries contributing positive after-cost PnL, capturing later winners that onset misses, or belonging to different provider episodes than the bar reconstruction. Revisit the rejected delays only under a separately pre-registered definition or independent forward evidence. Any access to sealed holdout metrics, same-bar fill, cost omission, changed evidence bytes, or execution authority invalidates this conclusion.
limitations: The evaluation is an independent-asset 15-minute approximation rather than shared-router wall-clock replay.
SPCX and GOLD validation profits become negative after removing their largest winner.
Development and validation have been used for exploration and are not a new sealed confirmation set.
The fast-EMA pullback definition was pre-specified but proved operationally too restrictive; it must not be loosened post hoc within this trial.
No live process, route, order, stop, target, position, size, allocation, leverage, or exit policy changed.
